name: Confuse enemies
summary: A gas, grenade, pulse or curse makes enemies in an area lose track of friend and foe for a few seconds. Their commander loses control of them and they attack whatever is near, which is usually their own side; some versions make them fire faster, or force them onto one chosen ally. Victims mostly spare the source and stay open to the user's fire, but in some versions a victim with no friend near turns on the user's side, and one version shields its victims from the user's team. It is short, works on an area and needs the enemy to be bunched up. Crewless machines, animals or psychic units are often immune, and units already busy with a target may ignore it. Taking command of an enemy is mind control; blocking sight is smoke.
counterplay: Spread out: a confused unit with no friend in reach can't hurt its own side, though in several versions it then simply fights the user's units, and one version ends early when no ally stays near the target.
Kill the carrier before it arrives: carriers are often unarmed and fragile, so turrets, aircraft and long-range fire stop them.
Field immune units: crewless robots and drones, animals and psychic units against the gas, and vehicle crews and garrisoned soldiers against the grenades.
Keep firing at a target: units already engaged may ignore a rage pulse until their target dies.
Back away from confused teammates and let the short timer run out.
Fight beside the user's own troops: confused enemies close to them shoot them too.

other_examples.unit: Confessor and Confessor cabal hallucinogenic grenades (Nod)
other_examples.note: Nod squad leaders lob a grenade on their own every few seconds that makes enemy soldiers in a small blast shoot each other for a few seconds; vehicle crews and garrisoned soldiers are safe from it. In Kane's Wrath the Confessor cabal throws the same grenade only on command, after a long wind-up. Each soldier hit turns on the others in his squad, and one with no ally in reach fights its enemies as usual while ignoring its commander.

An epic walker's ability makes every hostile near it fire on its own allies for a few seconds, vehicles and epic units included. Units already firing at something keep their target until it dies, defensive structures are not affected, and they shoot the raged units.

shooter_analogues.note: In a top-down game between players: freezes one enemy hero and forces its nearby allies to attack it, faster than usual. The frozen hero and the cursed allies take no harm from the caster's team apart from the caster's own magic, so the caster's team can't simply pile damage onto them.
A pulse makes enemies in a wide radius attack each other at random for a set time. Confused enemies still go for players who come too close, and each one sees an illusion of Nyx on the others.

A homing globule makes one enemy attack anyone around it for a short time, and the player if nobody else is near. Security robots and turrets are immune, and enemies that have hurt each other go on fighting after it wears off.

player_translation.summary: A fast, fragile carrier that slips into a bunched enemy group and vents a short-lived cloud. For a couple of seconds the enemies inside go berserk: their weapons fire by themselves at the nearest unit, usually a teammate, and faster than normal, but they keep control of their movement and can steer away. They never target you, but your own team must keep clear too.
as_user: Your gas deals no damage itself; its worth is in the crowd. Wait for the enemy to bunch up (a push through a choke point, a group around a tank), dive in, vent and get out.
You are fast and fragile: turrets, aircraft and long-range fire kill you on the way in, so approach from cover or behind a teammate.
Confused enemies never shoot you, but they do shoot your teammates nearby, so call the gas before you vent it.
Robots, drones and psychic units ignore the gas; save it for soldiers and crewed vehicles.
as_target: A hiss and a coloured cloud give you a moment to step out; touching the cloud again starts the clock over.
While berserk, your gun fires on its own at the nearest unit, faster than normal. You still steer, so turn and walk away from your teammates. Your HUD shows a countdown.
Teammates of a berserk player see a warning over them and should give space or take cover rather than shoot back; it is short.
teammates: The user's team follows the gas with a strike while the enemy fights itself, stays out of the berserk units' reach, and can carry the carrier in a transport for a surprise release.
The target's team spreads out, keeps turrets or anti-air covering choke points against the carrier, and fields immune units.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse fires a light weapon if the card has one.
Q: vent the cloud around you, on a short cooldown; the cloud lingers for a moment. One counted key.
Grenade variant: Q throws it toward the cursor after a short wind-up.
Victim: no shake-off, since the effect is short; hold X still bails out of a vehicle.
feedback: A coloured cloud with a clear edge on the ground, readable from above.
Berserk units get a pulsing red ring and an icon everyone can see, and their shots change colour so teammates know the fire is not on purpose.
The victim's HUD shows a short countdown, and their teammates see a berserk-ally marker on the minimap.
Immune units show the anti-control icon, and the gas visibly slides off them.
changes_from_rts: In Red Alert 2 the owner loses all command for several seconds; a player keeps movement here, and only the weapon goes berserk, for a shorter time.
Friendly fire has to be on for berserk shots only, and teammates killed by berserk fire should count as the gas user's kills, not the victim's fault.
The rule that victims never target the source stays, and the user's own team must be warned about the backfire.
RTS players mass tanks into a tight blob; shooter players spread out more, so the cloud needs a wider radius or a lingering zone to matter.
Immunities (robots, animals, psychic units) need icons that read from above.

team_play.notes: The gas is a setup: its value comes from the strike that follows while the enemy fights itself. The enemy answers with spacing, immune picks and cover against the carrier's approach.

notes: Forced fire at the nearest unit needs a target picker that skips the source; that part is simple.
A friendly-fire exception for berserk shots, and kill credit that goes to the gas user.
A lingering cloud that restarts the clock on contact.
Immunity checks by nature and class, and UI on both sides (countdown, berserk-ally markers).
Against a bunched team with a tank in the middle, a few seconds of self-fire can wipe it; duration and the fire-rate boost are the levers.
Teams that always spread out make it useless; radius and a lingering cloud tune that.
Taking a player's gun by force frustrates them, so keep it very short.
Players must tell a berserk ally from an enemy at once.
After a teamkill it must be clear who caused it, so nobody blames the victim.

variants.name: Berserk cloud
variants.summary: Vent a cloud around yourself; enemies inside fire faster at the nearest unit and never at you, and touching the gas again restarts their clock.

variants.name: Hallucinogen grenade
variants.summary: A thrown grenade with a small blast that makes soldiers shoot each other briefly; vehicle crews are sealed against it.
variants.seen_in: Tiberium Wars Confessor, Kane's Wrath Confessor cabal

counters.why: Squads of soldiers bunched behind cover shoot each other.

countered_by.why: Vehicle crews are sealed against the gas and can run the thrower down.
Long-range fire kills the thrower before it is close enough to throw.

variants.name: Single enrage
variants.summary: A homing shot makes one enemy attack anyone near it, and the user if it is alone, so the user must hit and hide.

variants.name: Friend-or-foe scramble
variants.summary: Victims keep full control, but their markers swap: allies show as enemies and enemies as allies, lock-ons pick allies, and friendly fire is on for them, so they must read the fight themselves.
variants.seen_in: An original player-facing twist; Warframe's Chaos shows the caster's illusion on confused enemies

adds_weaknesses.why: Short, and victims keep full control, so players who read the fight can still find your team; immune units ignore it.

variants.name: Lingering gas
variants.summary: The cloud stays on the ground for a while, so anyone who walks into it later is affected too.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Chaos Drone (the timer restarts on contact with the gas)

variants.name: Curse one ally
variants.summary: Freeze one enemy and force its nearby teammates to attack it; the frozen one and its cursed attackers are shielded from the user's team, so the curse can't be farmed.

variants.name: Rage pulse
variants.summary: A big unit's wide pulse reaches vehicles too; units already firing at a target keep it until it dies.

adds_strengths.why: Breaks up a bunched enemy group: for a few seconds they shoot each other instead of you.

adds_weaknesses.why: Short and tied to an area: spread-out enemies barely suffer, immune units ignore it, and confused enemies also fire on your nearby teammates.

counters.why: A massed vehicle push turns its guns on itself.
Frontline groups that brawl close together hit each other hardest.

countered_by.why: Robots and drones have no mind to confuse and can hunt the carrier freely.
Aircraft catch the carrier on its way in and stay out of the cloud.
Long-range fire kills the carrier before it reaches the group.

open_questions: Should berserk take a player's weapon (forced fire) or only scramble friend-and-foe markers?
Does berserk fire hurt teammates in modes without friendly fire, and who gets the kill?
Which units are immune in Shamble Frontlines: crewless machines only, or vehicles too, since their crews are sealed in?

shooter_fit.reason: Rewards reading the enemy's spacing and gives a dive-and-escape moment with a clear counter (spread out); taking a person's gun must stay very short, or use the marker-scramble variant.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. The wrong paths were fixed as the skeptic confirmed (cbe6de8).
